intended_object: The canonical A-algebra isomorphism between the localizations at w and at W, (A[w,x,y,z]/(wz−xy))[1/w] ≅ A[W,Y,T][1/W]. It is induced by the parametrization w↦W, x↦WT, y↦Y, z↦YT, with inverse W↦w, Y↦y, T↦x/w. This is the affine chart of the split quadric (cone) where w is invertible. I inferred this from the docstring, the module documentation and the surrounding chart section.
explanation:
The definition puts together two maps from earlier in the file:
- `chartForward`, the localization of the quotient map `phi` (w↦W, x↦WT, y↦Y, z↦YT), built with `IsLocalization.Away.mapₐ`;
- `chartBackward`, the extension of W↦w, Y↦y, T↦x·w⁻¹ to the localization, built with `IsLocalization.Away.liftAlgHom`.

The two inverse identities are proved in the file, and `AlgEquiv.ofAlgHom` combines everything into an A-algebra equivalence. This is exactly the standard chart isomorphism of the cone wz = xy over the open set {w ≠ 0}.

On generality:
- It is stated for an arbitrary commutative ring A, with no domain or nontriviality hypothesis.
- It works for any model LQ of the localization of the coordinate ring at w and any model LB of the localization of A[W,Y,T] at W. This is the most general formulation.
- The fixed variable counts (Fin 4 and Fin 3) are part of the specific object, so they do not make it too narrow.

Mathlib has no ready-made counterpart for this specific isomorphism.
